messages:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's runtime deploy we see a pretty big KV/prefix cache hit-rate delta between regions. us-west avg hit-rate ~78%, eu-central ~22%. Seems correlated with traffic routing + the new prefix canonicalization change.
kevin: ugh. which canonicalization change? the whitespace normalization patch?
maria: yeah, the PR that normalized whitespace + removed punctuation before hashing. Was meant to increase hit consolidation but might be causing key churn for some localized prompts.
alex: any profiling that points to causality? cache misses alone or also CPU uptick?
maria: both. Misses spiked first, then CPU for request path increased due to more cold KVs and downstream model warmup. Quick dump from /cache/stats: ```{\n  \"region\": \"eu-central\",\n  \"prefix_hit_rate\": 0.22,\n  \"kv_gets_per_s\": 430,\n  \"kv_misses_per_s\": 330\n}```
kevin: hmm 330 misses/s is significant. Is eviction rate high?
maria: eviction rate doubled in eu-central after deploy. LRU churn looks elevated.
sophie: are keys being partitioned differently now? canonicalization could change key distribution across shards if key-space hash changed.
pete: or could be routing — if eu traffic is being routed to a newer cluster with cold cache because we failed over last week. Any recent cluster resizes?
maria: there was a rolling upgrade in eu-central at 03:10 UTC. infra-bot logs show node replacement and re-sharding.
infra-bot: Deploy event: cluster-eu rollout started 2024-11-02T03:10:14Z; nodes replaced: 3; re-shard job triggered; status: complete.
alex: combining both factors sounds plausible: canonicalization changed keys, and re-shard caused cold cache. Two orthogonal causes amplify miss rates.
kevin: OK. What about warmup strategies? We have a hot-prefix prefetcher — did it target eu region?
maria: prefetcher uses historical top-k by region. Because canonicalization changed, the top-k mapping didn’t match the new keyspace, so prefetch didn't warm new keys.
sophie: Could we compute canonicalization mapping offline and generate warmup batches? e.g., replay last 24h prompts through new canonicalizer and prepopulate per-region caches.
pete: yes — we can run an offline job to materialize mapping and then push keys to kv using batch-put. Timeline?
kevin: before that, can we tweak routing to send eu-central reads to us-west if latency SLA allows? fallback routing would raise latency but preserve quality.
maria: measured p99 cross-region latency to us-west is +120ms — still within soft SLO for non-interactive endpoints. But several customers require <100ms. We can make it opt-in per route.
alex: also check cache keying: currently we key on sha256(prefix_normalized + model_id + quant_level). The normalization change may drop language-specific tokens. Maybe for eu we should include locale tag to avoid invalid collisions.
sophie: good point. Including locale may _increase_ key cardinality though. But we can do locale-aware warmup instead.
kevin: From perf side I saw a small regression in kernel selection around the same time — changed default kernel for matmul to fast-int8 path. That shouldn't affect KV, but it did change per-request CPU profile: more frequent context switches while waiting on cold cache.
pete: can you paste the flame graph snippet?
kevin: ```(flame graph snippet)\nmain->handle_request->kv_get (hot)->wait_on_io->kernel_int8_dispatch->...\nmain->handle_request->kv_get (cold)->model_load->kernel_compilation\n```
maria: actionable list? My proposal:
1) roll back canonicalization change on a canary (small percent) to validate effect.
2) run offline replay job to generate warmup keys per-region using post-canonicalization mapping.
3) for eu-central, temporarily increase cache capacity or pin hot shards to avoid eviction during rebuild.
4) add a routing rule to prefer local cache, but allow fallback to compatible region for non-SLA-critical routes.
5) collect detailed per-key hit-rate histograms and compare pre/post for 48h.
kevin: +1. Also run a perf profile focusing on kernel dispatch latency during cold hits vs warm hits.
sophie: I can own the warmup job and the per-key histograms. ETA: 8h for initial run, 24h to evaluate.
maria: I can do a canary rollback and coordinate with infra for shard pinning.
pete: I'll add an opt-in routing flag and a temporary traffic rule for eu we can flip.
alex: We'll need to notify a small set of customers about potential slight latency changes if we route cross-region. I'll draft a short note.
kevin: If rollback proves the canonicalizer is the culprit, let's add stricter unit tests for key stability and a migration path: maintain old->new mapping for X days with dual writes.
sophie: agreed. Dual-write + warmup is safest.
maria: ok team — plan set. I'll create a follow-up ticket and assign tasks. Thanks. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Ticket created: RI-1963 "eu prefix-cache hit-rate gap / warmup plan" assigned to maria,sophie,pete,kevin. Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RI-1963
